p|panel|borrado_lead: In almost every country with a data protection law, companies that keep your personal data have to delete it when you ask. This page helps you ask, with a letter ready to send that cites the law where you live.
p|panel|borrado_aviso_abogados: We are not lawyers: this is a template based on the law it cites.
p|panel|borrado_privado: Your name and email are only used to fill in the letters on this page. They are not saved in the ledger or in any GUARDIANA record, and GUARDIANA sends them to no one: you send the letter, from your own email. If you tick “Remember them in this browser”, they are kept only in this browser, on this computer.
p|panel|borrado_autoridad_lista: the data protection authority of your country (official list)
p|panel|borrado_autoridad_ninguna: there is no authority to complain to; see the note above.
p|panel|borrado_sin_derecho_limitado: Here the law gives no general right to have your data deleted. The letter asks for what it does give you: to know what they hold, to correct it, to withdraw your consent, and to have them destroy what they no longer need.
p|panel|borrado_sin_derecho_ninguno: Here no general law makes a company delete your data. The letter is a request, not a legal demand, and it says so.
p|panel|borrado_drop_titulo: If you live in California, start here
p|panel|borrado_drop_texto: The State of California runs an official, free platform, DROP, to ask every registered data broker to delete you in a single request. Since August 1, 2026 they must check it at least every 45 days. It is for California residents only.
p|panel|borrado_drop_enlace: Ask every data broker to delete you at once (DROP, official site)
p|panel|borrado_paso_empresa: 2. Pick the company and send the letter
p|panel|borrado_empresa_lead: At the top, the companies your home asked for, most first. Your home asking for their names doesn't mean they have your data: only they know, and the letter asks them.
p|panel|borrado_estado_cerrado: That business has closed: there is no one to write to.
p|panel|borrado_estado_incautado: Its website no longer belongs to it, by court order: there is no one to write to there.
p|panel|borrado_evidencia_frase: Your devices asked {n} times for {nombres} of {empresa}, between {desde} and {hasta}.
p|panel|borrado_evidencia_frase_uno: Your devices asked once for {nombres} of {empresa}, on {desde}.
p|panel|borrado_evidencia_nada: Your home hasn't asked for any of its names in what the ledger keeps.
p|panel|borrado_callados: {n} devices don't share their detail with the panel: what they asked for doesn't count here.
p|panel|borrado_callados_uno: 1 device doesn't share its detail with the panel: what it asked for doesn't count here.
p|panel|borrado_para: To: {correo} (the address the company itself publishes for this).
p|panel|borrado_sin_correo: This company publishes no email for this: you write to them through their privacy form.
p|panel|borrado_reloj_lead: Once you confirm you sent it, this is where you see how long they have left. Only the company, the place and the date are kept: not your name, not your email, not the letter.
p|panel|borrado_reloj_vacio: You haven't confirmed any letter yet.
p|panel|borrado_reloj_quedan: They have {n} days left: the deadline is {fecha}.
p|panel|borrado_reloj_quedan_uno: They have 1 day left: the deadline is {fecha}.
p|panel|borrado_reloj_vencido: The deadline passed on {fecha}, {n} days ago.
p|panel|borrado_reloj_vencido_uno: The deadline passed on {fecha}, 1 day ago.
p|panel|borrado_reloj_sin_plazo: The law sets no deadline here; we only note the day you sent it.
p|panel|borrado_reloj_prorroga: If they told you about an extension within the deadline, they can take until {fecha}.
p|panel|borrado_reloj_habiles: We count business days, Monday to Friday. GUARDIANA doesn't know your country's public holidays: the real deadline may fall a few days later.
p|panel|borrado_reloj_queja_titulo: They didn't answer in time: where to complain
p|panel|borrado_reloj_limite: Still seeing them on your network doesn't prove they didn't delete you. Deleting your data doesn't switch off their servers: your devices will keep asking for their names as long as a website or an app loads them. What proves they deleted you is their written answer.
p|panel|borrado_asunto_borrado: Request to delete my personal data — {empresa}
p|panel|borrado_asunto_limitado: Request for access, correction and deletion of my personal data — {empresa}
p|panel|borrado_asunto_ninguno: Request to delete my personal data — {empresa}
p|panel|borrado_carta_limitado:
To the privacy officer of {empresa}:

My name is {nombre}, and I am writing to you under {articulo} ({ley}).

I ask you to:
1. Tell me what personal data you hold about me, where you got it and who you have given it to.
2. Note that I withdraw any consent you understand I gave you to use, sell or share it.
3. Destroy the data you no longer need for the purpose you collected it for, and correct or delete any data that is inaccurate or incomplete.
4. Answer me in writing within {plazo}.

You can reply to this email address: {correo}. If you need any further detail to find me in your systems, let me know; I am not sending you more than necessary.
{evidencia}
{fecha}

{nombre}
p|panel|borrado_ley_es: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and Spain's Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPDGDD)
p|panel|borrado_articulo_es: Article 17 of the GDPR and Article 15 of the LOPDGDD
p|panel|borrado_plazo_es: one month from receipt of this request, extendable by two further months if you tell me why within the first month (Article 12(3) of the GDPR)
p|panel|borrado_nota_es: Ask the company first. If it doesn't answer within a month, or answers badly, you can file a complaint with the AEPD, free and online. If it is a debt register (ASNEF, Badexcug) and the debt is real, they may refuse to delete it while the law lets them keep it.
p|panel|borrado_queja_es: File a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) on its online portal. Attach the letter, the date you sent it and their answer, if any.
p|panel|borrado_ley_pt: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and Portugal's Law 58/2019
p|panel|borrado_plazo_pt: one month from receipt of this request, extendable by two further months if you tell me why within the first month (Article 12(3) of the GDPR)
p|panel|borrado_nota_pt: Ask the company first. If it doesn't answer within a month, you can file a complaint with the CNPD.
p|panel|borrado_queja_pt: File a complaint (participação) with Portugal's National Data Protection Commission (CNPD) on its website, with the letter, the date and their answer, if any.
p|panel|borrado_plazo_ie: one month from receipt of this request, extendable by two further months if you tell me why within the first month (Article 12(3) of the GDPR)
p|panel|borrado_nota_ie: Many big tech companies have their European headquarters in Ireland; their regulator is the Data Protection Commission (DPC).
p|panel|borrado_queja_ie: Write to the DPC through its web form, with copies of the letter and of the emails exchanged with the company, dates visible.
p|panel|borrado_plazo_ue: one month from receipt of this request, extendable by two further months if you tell me why within the first month (Article 12(3) of the GDPR)
p|panel|borrado_nota_ue: The GDPR is the same across the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. You complain to the authority of your own country; the European Data Protection Board publishes the list.
p|panel|borrado_queja_ue: Find your country's authority on the European Data Protection Board's list and file the complaint with the letter and the dates.
p|panel|borrado_ley_gb: UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018
p|panel|borrado_plazo_gb: one calendar month from receipt of this request, extendable by up to two further months if you tell me within the first month (Article 12(3) of the UK GDPR)
p|panel|borrado_nota_gb: The ICO asks you to complain to the company first and give it a chance to put things right. Since June 19, 2026 companies must acknowledge a complaint within 30 days.
p|panel|borrado_queja_gb: Complain to the company first. If you still get no answer, or it doesn't satisfy you, complain to the ICO on its website, with the letter and the dates.
p|panel|borrado_ley_us_ca: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), as amended by the CPRA
p|panel|borrado_plazo_us_ca: 45 days from receipt of this request, extendable once by 45 more if you tell me within the first 45 (section 1798.130)
p|panel|borrado_nota_us_ca: Section 1798.105 covers the data a business collected from you. For a broker that bought your data from others, DROP is the better way: one request to every registered broker, which since August 1, 2026 must process it every 45 days.
p|panel|borrado_queja_us_ca: File a complaint with the California Privacy Protection Agency (CalPrivacy) on its website.
p|panel|borrado_plazo_us_va: 45 days from receipt of this request, extendable once by 45 more if you tell me within the first 45 (section 59.1-577 B)
p|panel|borrado_nota_us_va: If the company says no, it must let you appeal and answer the appeal within 60 days; if it says no again, you can complain to the Attorney General.
p|panel|borrado_queja_us_va: Appeal to the company first. If it denies the appeal, file a complaint with the Virginia Attorney General.
p|panel|borrado_plazo_us_co: 45 days from receipt of this request, extendable by 45 more if you tell me and explain why (section 6-1-1306(2))
p|panel|borrado_nota_us_co: If the company doesn't answer or says no, you can complain to the Colorado Attorney General.
p|panel|borrado_queja_us_co: File a complaint on the Colorado Attorney General's data privacy portal.
p|panel|borrado_plazo_us_ct: 45 days from receipt of this request, extendable once by 45 more if you tell me within the first 45 (section 42-518(c))
p|panel|borrado_nota_us_ct: If it says no, you can appeal to the company; if it denies the appeal, complain to the Attorney General.
p|panel|borrado_queja_us_ct: On the Connecticut Attorney General's complaint form, choose “Consumer Data Privacy” and give the dates of your request, the denial and the appeal.
p|panel|borrado_plazo_us_ut: 45 days from receipt of this request, extendable once by 45 more if you tell me beforehand (section 13-61-203)
p|panel|borrado_nota_us_ut: In Utah the right to delete covers only the data you gave the company yourself; what a broker bought from others is left out.
